**(a)** Find \(I_{BQ}\), \(I_{CQ}\) and \(I_{EQ}\). [6]

**(b)** Find \(V_{CEQ}\) and show that the transistor is in the forward-active mode. [3]

**(c)** Write the equation of the DC load line, give its intercepts and sketch it with the Q-point. [4]

**(d)** Find the power dissipated in the transistor. [2]

**(e)** \(R_C\) is now increased while everything else stays the same. Find the largest \(R_C\) for which the transistor stays forward-active. [3]

**(a)** Base–emitter loop, assuming forward-active:

1. \(V_{BB} = I_B R_B + V_{BE(on)} + I_E R_E\) with \(I_E = (1+\beta) I_B\).
2. \(I_{BQ} = \dfrac{V_{BB} - 0.7}{R_B + (1+\beta)R_E} = \dfrac{2.3}{40\ \text{k} + (121)(1\ \text{k})} = \dfrac{2.3}{161\ \text{k}\Omega} = 14.29\ \mu\text{A}\).

2. \(I_B > 0\) and \(V_{CE} = 5.13\ \text{V} > V_{CE(sat)} = 0.2\) V, so the assumption holds: **forward-active**.

**(c)**

1. \(V_{CE} = V_{CC} - I_C\left(R_C + \tfrac{1+\beta}{\beta}R_E\right) = 12 - I_C(4.008\ \text{k}\Omega)\).
2. Intercepts: \(V_{CE} = 12\) V at \(I_C = 0\); \(I_C = 12/4.008 = 2.994\) mA at \(V_{CE} = 0\).
3. The Q-point \((5.13\ \text{V}, 1.714\ \text{mA})\) lies on the line.

**(d)** \(P_T = I_B V_{BE} + I_C V_{CE} = (14.29\ \mu\text{A})(0.7) + (1.714\ \text{mA})(5.13) = 8.80\) mW.

**(e)**

1. \(I_B\) does not depend on \(R_C\), so \(I_C = 1.714\) mA as long as the transistor is active.
2. The edge of saturation is \(V_{CE} = 0.2\) V: \(12 - I_C R_C - I_E R_E = 0.2\).
3. \(R_{C(max)} = \dfrac{12 - 0.2 - 1.729}{1.714} = 5.88\ \text{k}\Omega\).

**Answers:** \(I_{BQ} = 14.29\ \mu\text{A}\), \(I_{CQ} = 1.714\) mA, \(I_{EQ} = 1.729\) mA; \(V_{CEQ} = 5.13\) V (active); \(P_T = 8.80\) mW; \(R_C \le 5.88\ \text{k}\Omega\).

**(a)** Find \(I_{BQ}\), \(I_{EQ}\) and \(I_{CQ}\). [6]

**(b)** Find the emitter, base and collector voltages and \(V_{ECQ}\). Confirm the mode of operation. [4]

**(d)** Keeping \(R_B = 50\ \text{k}\Omega\), choose \(R_E\) so that \(I_{EQ} = 1\) mA. [4]
solution:
**(a)** Emitter–base loop from \(V^+\) to ground, assuming forward-active:

1. \(V^+ = I_E R_E + V_{EB(on)} + I_B R_B\), with \(I_E = (1+\beta)I_B\). (The base current flows *out* of the base, down through \(R_B\).)
2. \(I_{BQ} = \dfrac{5 - 0.7}{R_B + (1+\beta)R_E} = \dfrac{4.3}{50\ \text{k} + (91)(2\ \text{k})} = \dfrac{4.3}{232\ \text{k}\Omega} = 18.53\ \mu\text{A}\).
3. \(I_{EQ} = 91 I_{BQ} = 1.687\) mA, \(I_{CQ} = 90 I_{BQ} = 1.668\) mA.

**(b)**

1. \(V_E = 5 - I_E R_E = 5 - (1.687)(2) = 1.627\) V.
2. \(V_B = I_B R_B = (18.53\ \mu\text{A})(50\ \text{k}\Omega) = 0.927\) V (\(= V_E - 0.7\), as it must be).
3. \(V_C = -5 + I_C R_C = -5 + (1.668)(2.5) = -0.830\) V.
4. \(V_{ECQ} = V_E - V_C = 2.456\) V \(> 0.2\) V, and the base is above the collector, so the B–C junction is reverse biased: **forward-active**.

**(c)**

1. \(I_C\) stays \(1.668\) mA while active (the base loop does not contain \(R_C\)), and \(V_E\) stays \(1.627\) V.
2. Edge of saturation: \(V_C = V_E - 0.2 = 1.427\) V.
3. \(R_C = \dfrac{V_C - V^-}{I_C} = \dfrac{1.427 + 5}{1.668} = 3.85\ \text{k}\Omega\).

**(d)**

1. \(I_{BQ} = I_{EQ}/(1+\beta) = 1/91 = 10.99\ \mu\text{A}\).
2. Same loop: \(R_E = \dfrac{5 - 0.7 - I_{BQ}R_B}{I_{EQ}} = \dfrac{4.3 - (10.99\ \mu\text{A})(50\ \text{k}\Omega)}{1\ \text{mA}} = 3.751\ \text{k}\Omega\).

**Answers:** \(I_{BQ} = 18.53\ \mu\text{A}\), \(I_{EQ} = 1.687\) mA, \(I_{CQ} = 1.668\) mA; \(V_E = 1.627\) V, \(V_B = 0.927\) V, \(V_C = -0.830\) V, \(V_{ECQ} = 2.456\) V (active); \(R_C = 3.85\ \text{k}\Omega\) at the edge; \(R_E = 3.751\ \text{k}\Omega\).

**(a)** With \(V_{BB} = 4\) V and \(R_B = 33\ \text{k}\Omega\), use the assume-then-check method to find the mode of operation, \(I_B\), \(I_C\) and \(V_{CE}\). Give the forced \(\beta\). [6]

**(b)** Find the power dissipated in the transistor for (a). [2]

**(c)** With \(V_{BB} = 4\) V, what range of \(R_B\) keeps the transistor forward-active? [3]

**(d)** Find the Q-point for \(R_B = 100\ \text{k}\Omega\) and \(V_{BB} = 4\) V. [3]

**(e)** With \(R_B = 33\ \text{k}\Omega\), find the value of \(V_{BB}\) at which the transistor just enters saturation. [2]
solution:
**(a)**

1. Assume forward-active: \(I_B = \dfrac{4 - 0.7}{33\ \text{k}\Omega} = 100.0\ \mu\text{A}\), so \(I_C = \beta I_B = 11.00\) mA.
2. Then \(V_{CE} = 9 - (11.00)(1.5) = -7.50\) V, which is negative: impossible, so the assumption fails.
3. Assume saturation: \(V_{CE} = 0.2\) V, \(I_C = \dfrac{9 - 0.2}{1.5\ \text{k}\Omega} = 5.867\) mA. \(I_B = 100.0\ \mu\text{A}\) is unchanged (the base loop does not involve the collector).
4. Check: \(\beta I_B = 11.00\ \text{mA} > I_{C(sat)} = 5.867\) mA, so the transistor is **saturated**.
5. Forced \(\beta = I_C/I_B = 5.867/0.1000 = 58.7\), less than 110.

**(b)** \(P_T = I_B V_{BE} + I_C V_{CE(sat)} = (0.1000)(0.7) + (5.867)(0.2) = 1.243\) mW.

**(c)**

1. Active needs \(\beta I_B < I_{C(sat)}\): \(I_B < 5.867/110 = 53.33\ \mu\text{A}\).
2. \(R_B > \dfrac{4 - 0.7}{53.33\ \mu\text{A}} = 61.88\ \text{k}\Omega\).

**(d)**

1. \(I_B = 3.3/100\ \text{k} = 33.0\ \mu\text{A}\); \(I_C = 110 \times 33.0\ \mu\text{A} = 3.63\) mA.
2. \(V_{CE} = 9 - (3.63)(1.5) = 3.555\) V \(> 0.2\) V: active. Q-point \((3.56\ \text{V}, 3.63\ \text{mA})\).

**(e)** Saturation starts when \(I_B = 53.33\ \mu\text{A}\): \(V_{BB} = 0.7 + (53.33\ \mu\text{A})(33\ \text{k}\Omega) = 2.460\) V.

**Answers:** saturated, \(I_B = 100.0\ \mu\text{A}\), \(I_C = 5.867\) mA, \(V_{CE} = 0.2\) V, \(\beta_{forced} = 58.7\); \(P_T = 1.243\) mW; \(R_B > 61.88\ \text{k}\Omega\); Q \(= (3.56\ \text{V}, 3.63\ \text{mA})\); \(V_{BB} = 2.460\) V.

**(c)** Choose \(V_{BB}\) for the largest symmetrical output swing, and find \(V_{OQ}\) and the largest output amplitude. [4]

**(e)** The transistor is replaced by one with \(\beta = 100\), with the same \(V_{BB}\). Find the new \(V_{OQ}\) and the largest input amplitude before the output clips. Which side clips first? [3]

**(a)** \(A_v = -\dfrac{\beta R_C}{R_B} = -\dfrac{(125)(4)}{100} = -5.0\).

**(b)**

1. Lower edge: the transistor turns on at \(v_I = 0.7\) V.
2. Upper edge: saturation at \(v_O = 0.2\) V, i.e. \(v_I = 0.7 + \dfrac{V^+ - 0.2}{|A_v|} = 0.7 + \dfrac{9.8}{5} = 2.66\) V.
3. Active for \(0.7 < v_I < 2.66\) V.

**(c)**

1. The middle of that range: \(V_{BB} = (0.7 + 2.66)/2 = 1.68\) V.
2. \(V_{OQ} = 10 - 5(1.68 - 0.7) = 5.10\) V.
3. The input can swing \(\pm0.98\) V, so the output swings \(\pm4.90\) V (from 0.2 V to 10 V).

**(d)** \(v_O = 5.10 - 5(0.3\sin\omega t) = 5.10 - 1.5\sin\omega t\) V, inverted and within the limits.

**(e)**

1. \(A_v = -(100)(4)/100 = -4\); \(V_{OQ} = 10 - 4(1.68 - 0.7) = 6.08\) V.
2. Cutoff is still \(0.98\) V below \(V_{BB}\); saturation is now at \(v_I = 0.7 + 9.8/4 = 3.150\) V, \(1.47\) V above it.
3. Largest input amplitude \(= 0.98\) V (output amplitude \(3.92\) V). The output clips first at the **top** (cutoff, \(v_O = 10\) V): the Q-point is no longer centred.

**Answers:** \(A_v = -5.0\); active for \(0.7 < v_I < 2.66\) V; \(V_{BB} = 1.68\) V, \(V_{OQ} = 5.10\) V, \(\pm4.90\) V; \(v_O = 5.10 - 1.5\sin\omega t\) V; \(V_{OQ} = 6.08\) V, \(\pm0.98\) V in, cutoff side clips first.

**(d)** \(P = I_DV_{DS} = (20)(0.3258) = 6.52\) mW.
